notes: 2026-01-25: Intro call (Aisha). Product + infra overview. They run a mid-market ITSM product used by ~600 customers.

Use case summary: internal IT/helpdesk chatbot for agents + first-line triage. Primary goal: reduce time-to-resolution for internal tickets and surface runbook snippets to agents. Must support tool calling (ticket updates, escalation) and streaming responses for snappy UX.

Latency SLO: Head of Product quoted 'must feel instant' — target median <= 250ms for short turn replies, P95 < 700ms for streaming token pipeline. Concerned about tail spikes during peak shift changes.

Security & compliance: require SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs with immutable retention, retention controls per-tenant (1 year default), ability to redact PII from logs. Prefer KMS integration for key management. Data residency: US only for customer metadata; logs can be multi-region with controls.

2026-02-10: Hosted API demo. Showed streaming + tool calling. Product liked streaming SDK and function-call style integration. Raised question: what happens on model fallback mid-stream? Need deterministic behavior for agent UI.
2026-02-28: Security review with Security Ops. Sent SRD and asked for SOC2 Type II and remediation plan for historical log access. Drive: security Qs doc attached.

2026-03-05: POC kickoff (hosted). POC scope: 2-week internal helpdesk bot, 5k messages/day simulated, integrate with internal ticketing via lambda tool-calls. Measure median/P95 latency, error rate, and token cost per session.

2026-03-08: POC result snapshot: median latency 240ms (good), P95 ~900ms during peak — root-cause seems to be batching + KV-cache warmup. SE working with infra to adjust batching window and early prefix caching. Recorded Fireflies ff-0a3b4c.

Pricing conversation: prefer to start on hosted pay-as-you-go for quick rollout. If sustained QPS > X, they want a path to Dedicated with committed throughput pricing. Ask: sample committed tiers and overage behavior.
Quote from Head of Product: 'If agents feel even a half-second lag we lose buy-in; streaming + immediate token flush is a must.'
Operational needs: supportable rollout cadence (canary by team), token-level cost visibility, per-route dashboards. Want Redwood Console demos for tracing and rollouts.

Open engineering asks: 1) formal guarantee on streaming interruptions and how fallback to smaller model is surfaced to UI, 2) SLA for Dedicated option (latency targets), 3) log retention controls UI/API.

Next steps: deliver POC findings doc, propose pricing scenarios (hosted vs committed Dedicated), security artifacts (SOC2/ISO) to procurement. Schedule follow-up week of 2026-03-15 to review proposed Dedicated tier.
Procurement rhythm: procurement starts once security artifacts validated. Procurement lead expects 4-6 weeks lead time for contracts if Dedicated chosen.

Notes: They ran a competitor PoC (ServiceNow MLP) last year; main differentiator is latency & tool-calling reliability. They want references of similar mid-market customers using Dedicated for internal chatbots.
